question: Do actual Triton compiler/cache-call intervals coincide with the unexplained layer0 long host calls in a short-warmup uniform pager finite cohort?

modes.uniform: Same ordinary expert grouping, fixed24 slots/layer in both engines

warmup.state: Default non-injection/non-same-engine first-request warmup, full completion before measurement; per-policy expert cache retained, no measurement reset. Warmup requests/KV drain; completed request KV is naturally freed, prefix caching disabled.
warmup.jit_scope: One short warmup does not establish all shapes are warmed; any later compilation remains in measured/process costs.

experiment_unit: Two fresh U engines, same 16-document finite cohort. First uses a new empty private Triton disk cache, second retains exactly that cache; each process has fresh in-memory compiled handles. Order and time are confounded; this is source localization, not a performance estimate.
primary: Per compiler invocation cache metadata outcome and elapsed host interval
Overlap with exact ordinary-pager call_id, layer, phase and shape; actual host_apply and engine.step intervals
secondary: arrival-based per-request TTFT and completion latency
actual expert+KV bytes and CUDA peak allocated/reserved
entire subprocess wall including initialization,warmup,capture,finalize,IO and shutdown
accounting: Capture excludes prior warmup/setup and following finalization/shutdown; full subprocess wall retains all.
No cycle_complete or runtime GC observer in reused single-capture branch; memory trace retention stays until finalize, with cost retained.
Do not sum nested host/CUDA/apply spans into wall. Include actual preemption/recomputation, failures and every cell; no subtraction of warmup/observer/IO costs.

Clock arrivals are submitted between synchronous engine steps. Arrival lag is distinct from native queue waiting; cohort capture includes the initial arrival transient and final drain, but excludes engine startup. This finite cohort is not steady-state.
boundaries: Same-model/source/resources/input and single warmup as finite_arrival_r01; no F/X retuning, new controller or reference kernel.
Instrumentation runs in both cells and its cost is retained; newly instrumented times are not directly compared to old uninstrumented performance.
Every attempt and both cells retained, stop on exception/incomplete output; no automatic retry or cache reset.
Use common advisory flock for entire two-cell group plus queue handoff and pre-cell GPU UUID/emptiness checks. Busy/query failure aborts. Common lock cannot constrain an uncooperative process.
A d6 conditional group is preceding queue position; no launch during another group or an inter-cell gap.
Source-localization result may identify actual cache compile/load stalls, or leave host work unresolved. No positive result is required.

jit_cache.initial: Created empty by this driver with exist_ok=False
jit_cache.second: Same directory and all first-run files retained; inventory before/after each process
jit_cache.other_caches: Existing CUDA/FlashInfer/torch caches are not deleted or declared cold. Only the Triton disk-cache initial state is manipulated.
jit_cache.interpretation: An invocation of compile() may load a disk-cached binary; distinguish metadata hit/miss. Its host envelope also contains lookup/load work. Do not call every invocation compilation or sum nested intervals.

observer.intervals: pager_apply, compiler_call, launcher_and_driver_load; native compiler listener cache_hit differentiates pipeline and disk load
observer.unknowns: Unwrapped listener events, failures, missing parent/shape or trace joins produce analysis issues; startup events without active apply remain unattributed
observer.cost: All instrumentation/process costs retained; no GPU synchronization added; nested host intervals use unions
